newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada board approves north pipeline abandonment.
newsitem.headline: Canada board approves north pipeline abandonment.

text.p: Canada's National Energy Board said on Monday it approved an application by the owner of a refined products pipeline built in Canada's far north during World War II to abandon the line.

Yukon Pipelines Ltd, a unit of Russel Metals Inc, wants to abandon the 144.5 km (90 mile) Canadian section of the 177-km (110-mile) Canol pipeline. The Canadian section extends to Whitehorse, Yukon from the British Columbia-Alaska border.
The company applied in July 1995 to abandon the facilities, which also consist of a tank farm in Whitehorse and a pump station near Carcross, Yukon.
A public hearing on the application was held in Whitehorse last month.
The NEB said the company estimates the cost of removing the pipe, dismantling storage tanks and conducting environmental assessments and remediation at C$1.6 million.
It said the cost would be offset by sale of the pipe, tanks and land occupied by the upper tank farm in Whitehorse.
The Yukon Pipeline system was originally part of an extensive northern pipeline system built by the United States Army in 1942.
After the war, the portion between Skagway, Alaska and Whitehorse remained in operation, transporting refined petroleum products. It was deactiviated in 1994. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
